battle.name: 多米尼加共和國獨立戰爭
battle.theater: 伊斯帕尼奧拉島中北部與聖多明各
battle.brief: 一八四三年三月十六日杜阿特在聖多明各創立三一社，號召驅逐海地二十二年的佔領；同年春起義在北部爆發，十一月六日於塔蘭克雷擊敗海地縱隊，杜阿特旋即在拉雷斯被俘。一八四四年海地新政府同意撤軍，聖多明各易旗。卡面那支一八四〇年法國雷管步槍並未登陸此島，起義軍用的仍是舊式燧發火槍。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 海地一方是海地共和國的佔領當局。一八二二年二月，總統讓・皮埃爾・博瓦耶以「維護新獨立方島上秩序」的名義出兵，進駐西班牙聖多明各的東部，此後二十二年，島的東半部置於海地軍政之下。佔領軍的編制以步兵線列為主，配輕野砲連與騎兵，另有小型縱帆砲艇沿北部海岸巡弋封鎖；聖多明各城由海軍陸戰隊與駐防軍看守，聖地亞哥等內陸城鎮設軍事駐地。一八四三年在位的總統夏爾・利維耶爾・埃拉爾同時握有國家與軍隊的權柄，他主張海地是西屬島嶼獨立的「保障國」，並在太子港集結大軍，準備向北遠征。多米尼加一方是一八四三年三月十六日在聖多明各秘密成立的三一社及其武裝，骨幹是杜阿特、魯伊斯、埃斯帕利亞特等舊西班牙時期的軍人與知識分子，另有莊園武裝、獵人、農民兵與一批由外地購回而數量不多的步槍；起義初期分散成數百人的游擊隊，其後在北部集中成解放軍，並以舊式軍官為核心組織地方民兵。外援方面，起義方與委內瑞拉的玻利瓦爾圈子保持聯繫，購槍與運人主要走委內瑞拉與古巴的航線；島嶼周邊同時存在英美商人主導的軍火黑市，軍械在太子港與外港之間轉手，而海地一方的佔領當局正是這條黑市最大的買家與賣家。
countriesEn: One side was the occupying authority of the Republic of Haiti. In February 1822 President Jean-Pierre Boyer sent troops into the eastern part of Spanish Santo Domingo under the pretext of keeping order on an island whose independence had just been recognised, and for the next twenty-two years the eastern half of the island was placed under Haitian military government. The occupying order of battle was built around infantry in line, supported by light field-gun batteries and cavalry, with small schooners mounting guns patrolling the northern coast as a blockade; the city of Santo Domingo was watched by marines and a garrison, and inland towns such as Santiago held military stations. The president in office in 1843, Charles Rivière-Hérard, held the state and the army in the same hands: he proclaimed Haiti the guarantor of the island's independence from Spain, and he mustered a large force at Port-au-Prince for a campaign to the north. The Dominican side was the Trinitarian Society, secretly founded at Santo Domingo on 16 March 1843, together with its armed bands. Its core was Juan Pablo Duarte, Félix María Ruiz, José María Espaillat and other officers and intellectuals of the former Spanish colonial order, joined by plantation militias, hunters, farmer levies and a small number of muskets bought from abroad; the rising began as dispersed bands of a few hundred men and was later concentrated in the north into a Liberation Army, with local militias organised around old Spanish officers. For foreign support the insurgents kept in touch with the circle around Simón Bolívar in Venezuela, and the purchase and transport of arms ran mainly through the Venezuelan and Cuban routes; at the same time a British and American merchant network traded muskets and intelligence around the island, and the Haitian occupying authorities were both the largest buyers and the largest sellers on that market.
people: 雙方的核心人物集中在幾個點上。多米尼加方面，一八一四年生於聖多明各的胡安・巴布蒂斯塔・杜阿特是三一社的靈魂人物，他一八二四年自委內瑞拉返國後先組建慈善會，一八四三年三月十六日與費利克斯・瑪麗亞・魯伊斯、何塞・瑪麗亞・埃斯帕利亞特等人秘密成立三一社，此後以解放軍總指揮的身分在北部作戰，一八四三年十一月六日於塔蘭克雷取勝，十三十三日卻在拉雷斯被嚮導出賣而被俘，關至次年海地政局變動後始獲釋放；他後於一八四六年二月出任政府首長，一八六五年復國戰爭中再任總統，一八六六年五月二十日遇刺身亡。魯伊斯是三一社共同創辦人兼解放軍副手，據方志記載於一八四三年十一月陣亡；埃斯帕利亞特是南美洲獨立戰爭的老兵，在解放軍中任副手，專責訓練與編制。胡安・亞歷杭德羅・阿科斯塔是北部的主要軍事指揮官，塔蘭克雷一役中與杜阿特並肩作戰，日後成為一八六五年復國運動的領袖之一；曼紐埃爾・德・雷格拉・莫塔、何塞・馬里亞・因貝特與馬蒂亞斯・拉蒙・梅利亞分別在東部、聖地亞哥與鄉村組織武裝，其中因貝特以法律人的身分起草起義方的文告，梅利亞帶領東部的鄉民武裝加入。康比亞索則扮演商人的角色：他受命赴委內瑞拉購運軍械，成為起義方最實際的後勤線之一。海地方面，總統夏爾・利維耶爾・埃拉爾是佔領軍的最高決策者，他的政權以混血裔自由人為骨幹，與黑人派系互相猜忌；一八四四年五月他被暗殺後，太子港改由讓・皮埃爾・拉蒂耶爾主持，並與起義方議定撤軍。將領方面，讓・路易・皮埃羅與佩德羅・歐亨尼奧・佩爾蒂埃先後在北線作戰，其中佩爾蒂埃正是塔蘭克雷一役的敗方指揮者；日後的索盧克在位期間更兩度大舉入侵，把這場島內衝突推成國際事件。
peopleEn: The central figures of both sides cluster around a handful of men. On the Dominican side Juan Pablo Duarte, born at Santo Domingo in 1814, was the soul of the Trinitarian Society. After returning from Venezuela in 1824 he first set up the Filantrópica, and on 16 March 1843 he secretly founded the Trinitarian Society with Félix María Ruiz, José María Espaillat and others; he then fought in the north as commander-in-chief of the Liberation Army, won the action at Talanquera on 6 November 1843, and was captured on 13 November at Lares after being betrayed by his guide, remaining in prison until the change of government in Haiti the following year. He later became head of government in February 1846, was president once more during the Restoration War of 1865, and was assassinated on 20 May 1866. Ruiz was the co-founder of the Trinitarian Society and second-in-command of the Liberation Army, and the local chronicles record him as killed in action in November 1843. Espaillat was a veteran of the wars of Spanish American independence and served as deputy commander in the Liberation Army, responsible for training and organisation. Juan Alejandro Acosta was the principal military commander in the north, fought shoulder to shoulder with Duarte at Talanquera, and later became one of the leaders of the Restoration movement of 1865. Manuel de Regla Mota, José María Imbert and Matías Ramón Mella organised armed bands in the east, at Santiago and in the countryside respectively; Imbert, a lawyer, drafted the insurgents' proclamations, and Mella brought the armed villagers of the eastern provinces into the rising. Cambiaso played the merchant's part: he was sent to Venezuela to purchase and transport arms and became one of the insurgents' most practical lines of supply. On the Haitian side the president Charles Rivière-Hérard was the highest decision-maker of the occupying army; his regime rested on the free people of colour while mistrusting the black faction, and after he was assassinated in May 1844 Port-au-Prince was run by Jean-Pierre Latortue, who came to terms with the insurgents on a withdrawal. Among the generals, Jean-Louis Pierrot and Pedro Eugenio Pelletier operated on the northern front, and Pelletier was the defeated commander at Talanquera; Soulouque, who came to power later, invaded the island twice, turning what had been a civil conflict on one island into an international affair.
kits: 卡面這支一八四〇年的法國雷管步槍是一張年代卡：它是歐洲最早一批量產的雷管前裝步槍，口徑約十七毫米、槍管無膛線、配紙包彈，以底火取代火燧，濕霧天氣也能擊發——但它並沒有出現在這場戰爭裡。島上雙方實際使用的，是西班牙殖民時代留下的燧發滑膛步槍與獵槍，口徑多在十四至十五毫米上下，火藥或散裝或以紙分裝，銅帽與火藥在雨季極易受潮，擊砧與火燧一旦受潮便成啞火，這正是雷管當年要解決的難題，而多米尼加直到一八六五年都沒有條件換裝。起義軍的冷兵器以砍刀、長矛與斧頭為主，槍械彈藥靠突擊徵用與零星外購，缺口極大；海地軍的裝備整齊得多，配備線列步槍、數百磅級的輕野砲、馬刀騎兵與少量手槍，並以小型縱帆砲艇在北部海岸攔截漁船與走私船。兩邊都靠驃馬隊與牛車作運輸，海地軍的糧食由太子港與南部港口分批北運，起義方則以破壞這條補給線為主要戰術。攻城與守城的器材也在場：聖地亞哥有城牆、砲台、街壘與柴拒馬，起義方一度以少量舊式銅砲支援城防。槍械的譜系更值得記一筆：夏斯波一八四〇年型的點火機構，日後演成一八六六年步槍，再成勒貝爾步槍的祖型；而一八六五年復國戰爭的雙方都已用上進口的雷管前裝步槍與左輪手槍，射擊質量與一八四三年完全不可同日而語。
kitsEn: The percussion rifle of 1840 on this card is a period card: it belongs to the first generation of mass-produced percussion muzzle-loading muskets in Europe, with a bore of about seventeen millimetres, no rifling, paper cartridges, and a primer that replaced the flint, so that it would fire in damp fog. It did not, however, take part in this war. What the two sides actually carried on the island were flintlock smoothbore muskets and shotguns left over from the Spanish colonial period, of bores mostly around fourteen to fifteen millimetres, with powder either loose or divided into paper cartridges; the flints and powder were very easily spoiled by the rainy season, and a damp frizzen or damp powder meant a silent misfire. This was precisely the problem percussion ignition was invented to solve, and the Dominicans had no means of refitting their arms until 1865. The cold weapons of the insurgents were machetes, long lances and axes; their muskets and ammunition came from sudden seizures and occasional purchases abroad, and the gap was never closed. The Haitian troops were far better equipped by comparison, with line muskets, light field guns in the several-hundred-pound class, sabre cavalry and a few pistols, and they used small schooner gunboats on the northern coast to stop fishing boats and smuggling craft. Both sides moved its supplies by mule trains and ox carts; the Haitian grain came north in batches from Port-au-Prince and the southern ports, and the insurgents made breaking that supply line their main tactical aim. Siege and defence material was present as well: Santiago had its walls, batteries, barricades and gabions, and the insurgents supported the town's defence for a time with a few old bronze pieces. The lineage of the weapon deserves a note as well: the ignition system of the Chassepot pattern of 1840 grew into the musket of 1866 and then into the ancestor of the Lebel; and by the Restoration War of 1865 both sides were already using imported percussion muzzle-loading rifles and revolvers, so that the quality of shooting had become incomparable with that of 1843.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以分三段來看。第一段是一八四三年春到夏的零星起事：起義方兵力分散、槍械缺乏，只能靠夜襲、伏擊與破壞道路通信來拖延，設法讓海地軍的縱隊在內陸多山的地形上反覆行軍，把對方的行列拉長。第二段是同年秋天的會戰：起義方在北部集中人馬，十一月六日在塔蘭克雷與海地縱隊交戰，利用科迪耶拉中脈與尤納河谷一帶的丘陵、密林與溪流，把以縱隊行軍的敵軍切割成數段，再從側翼以近距離火力與砍刀衝鋒打散其陣形，隨後切斷其退路與輜重；這是整場戰爭唯一一次大規模野戰，也是一八四三年起義方唯一的戰術性勝利。第三段是一八四四年海地軍的反攻：雙方在聖地亞哥、北部走廊與東部鄉村反覆拉鋸，起義方以守城、郊區游擊與襲擊敵方後勤隊對抗縱隊式進攻，靠人少而地熟拖延消耗。整場戰爭的技術難題同時就是戰術難題：雨季的濕熱令火藥受潮、槍械啞火，道路泥濘令輜重隊寸步難行，起義方一旦離開森林與鄉村，進入開闊的亞沃拉大平原與聖地亞哥盆地，在海地軍的砲火與騎兵面前便毫無辦法——這正是缺少雷管槍與重砲所帶來的差距。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this war fall into three phases. The first is the scattered rising of the spring and summer of 1843: the insurgents were few and badly armed, so they could only fall back on night attacks, ambushes and the destruction of roads and communications in order to delay the enemy and to keep Haitian columns marching in a mountainous interior, stretching them out. The second phase is the pitched action of the autumn of that year: the insurgents concentrated their men in the north and on 6 November fought a Haitian column at Talanquera, using the hills, dense woods and streams of the Cordillera Central and the Yuna valley to cut an army marching in column into several separate bodies, then breaking their formations from the flank with close-range fire and charges with machetes, and finally cutting their retreat and their baggage train. This was the only large field action of the whole war and the only tactical victory the insurgents won in 1843. The third phase is the Haitian counter-offensive of 1844: the two sides fought up and down over Santiago, the northern corridor and the eastern countryside, the insurgents meeting columnar attacks with the defence of towns, mounted work in the outskirts and raids on enemy supply columns, wearing the enemy down through their small numbers and their intimate knowledge of the ground. The technical difficulty of the war was at the same time its tactical difficulty: the damp heat of the rainy season spoiled the powder and silenced the muskets, and mud on the roads crippled the baggage trains; once the insurgents left the forests and villages and came out onto the open plain of the Yuna and the basin of Santiago, they had nothing whatever against Haitian gunfire and cavalry. That was the gap left by having neither percussion muskets nor heavy guns.
data: 時間與日期方面：一八二一年十二月一日，聖多明各以東的西班牙屬地宣布脫離西班牙並成立軍政府；一八二二年二月海地出兵佔領，佔領持續到一八四四年，前後二十二年；一八二四年杜阿特返國；一八二五年成立慈善會；一八四三年三月十六日三一社成立，同年春夏起義在北部與東部接連爆發，十一月六日塔蘭克雷之戰，十三十三日杜阿特在拉雷斯被俘；一八四四年五月海地總統遇刺、拉蒂耶爾執政，年末雙方議定撤軍；一八四五年多米尼加成立臨時政府；一八四六年二月杜阿特出任政府首長；一八四七年索盧克當選海地總統，一八四九年自立為帝並大舉入侵；一八五五年海地與西班牙開戰；一八六五年復國戰爭爆發；一八六六年五月二十日杜阿特遇刺。兵員方面，起義方的常見記載是每次地方起事只有數百人，能一次集中到數千人的會戰在整個系列戰事中屈指可數；海地一方則長期維持一萬人上下的常備與民兵，遠征時出動的縱隊通常也有數千人，兩造在塔蘭克雷一役的兵力大致相當，但海地一方有砲。損失與補給方面，兩造都沒有留下可靠的總傷亡冊，起義方的零星戰史常只記首領陣亡與少量被俘的數目；可以確定的只是軍械消耗：熱帶雨季令火藥與槍械報廢的速度極快，起義軍的槍枝長期靠突擊徵用與零星外購維持，缺口從未填平。距離上，聖多明各至聖地亞哥的陸路約二百公里，中間橫跨三條大河與多個山口，是雙方爭奪的走廊；海地軍每一次北進都要維持這條線，海地方面的失血正是沿著這條線發生。
dataEn: On dates and timing: on 1 December 1821 the Spanish provinces east of Santo Domingo declared their independence from Spain and formed a military government; in February 1822 Haiti invaded and the occupation lasted until 1844, twenty-two years in all; Duarte returned in 1824; the Filantrópica was founded in 1825; the Trinitarian Society was founded on 16 March 1843, with risings breaking out in the north and the east during the spring and summer of that year, the action at Talanquera on 6 November and Duarte's capture at Lares on 13 November; in May 1844 the Haitian president was assassinated and Latortue took over, and at the end of the year the two sides agreed on a withdrawal; a provisional Dominican government was set up in 1845; Duarte became head of government in February 1846; Soulouque was elected president of Haiti in 1847 and proclaimed himself emperor and invaded in 1849; Haiti went to war with Spain in 1855; the Restoration War broke out in 1865; and Duarte was assassinated on 20 May 1866. On numbers: the usual account of the insurgents is that each local rising numbered only a few hundred men, and that actions in which several thousand were concentrated at once are rare in the whole series of battles; the Haitian side maintained a standing force and militia of around ten thousand men, and the columns it sent north on campaign usually numbered several thousand, so that the two sides at Talanquera were roughly matched in strength, though the Haitians had guns. On losses and supply: neither side left reliable overall casualty returns, and the scanty Dominican chronicles record only the deaths of leaders and small numbers taken prisoner; what can be stated with confidence is the consumption of arms and ammunition, for the tropical rains ruined powder and muskets very quickly, and the insurgents' firearms were maintained by seizure and by occasional purchase abroad, a gap that was never closed. On distance: the land road from Santo Domingo to Santiago is about two hundred kilometres and crosses three great rivers and several passes, and it was the corridor both sides fought for; every Haitian advance north had to keep that line open, and that is where Haiti's losses were suffered.
cause: 打起來的原因是三層。最遠的一層是西班牙的崩解：一八二一年西班牙美洲戰爭全面崩盤，聖多明各以東宣布自治並成立軍政府，又致書海地求援，海地藉此取得對島嶼東半部的「保障」地位；出兵的理由，是怕西班牙或歐洲列強捲土重來，也擔心聖多明各落入英法荷等海權之手。但佔領之後，這份「保障」就變成了一紙永久的佔領令，島的東西兩半分屬兩個國家。第二層是海地內部的權力鬥爭：佔領當局靠沒收西班牙王室與教會的產業維持開支，把東部的土地一批批賣給海地商人與軍人，多米尼加原住民對此長期不滿；同時海地本國的黑人與混血派系互不信任，一八四二年掌權的埃拉爾清洗了混血裔軍官，這使佔領軍內部的凝聚力在關鍵時刻打了折扣。第三層是起義方自身的準備：一八二〇年代起，杜阿特等人便在委內瑞拉與古巴之間活動，把南美洲獨立戰爭的經驗、玻利瓦爾的共和理想與共濟會式的秘密組織帶回島上，一八二五年的慈善會是一層掩護，一八四三年三月十六日的三一社才是真正的起義機關；隨後北部與東部的起事同時爆發，才把醞釀了二十年的不滿變成公開的戰爭。
causeEn: There are three layers behind the fighting. The farthest is the collapse of Spain: in 1821 the Spanish American wars came apart entirely, the provinces east of Santo Domingo declared their autonomy and formed a military government, and they wrote to Haiti for help, which gave Haiti the position of guarantor over the eastern half of the island. The reason for the invasion was the fear that Spain or a European power might come back, and the fear that Santo Domingo might fall to Britain, France or the Netherlands. But once the occupation was under way, that guarantee became a permanent order of dispossession, with the island split between two countries. The second layer is the struggle for power inside Haiti: the occupation paid for itself by confiscating Spanish royal and ecclesiastical property and selling off the land of the east in parcels to Haitian merchants and soldiers, and the people of the original eastern provinces resented it for a long time; at the same time the black and the free-people-of-colour factions in Haiti did not trust each other, and when Rivière-Hérard took power in 1842 he purged the officers of mixed race, which told badly on the cohesion of the occupying army at the decisive moment. The third layer is the preparation of the insurgents themselves: from the 1820s Duarte and his companions moved between Venezuela and Cuba, carrying back to the island the experience of the South American wars of independence, the republican ideals of Bolívar, and a secret organisation of a masonic kind; the Filantrópica of 1825 was one layer of cover, and the Trinitarian Society of 16 March 1843 was the real engine of the revolt. When risings in the north and the east broke out at the same time, twenty years of resentment were turned into open war.
impact: 直接後果是海地對東部的二十二年佔領結束。一八四四年七月十九日，聖多明各主教座堂的鐘聲被敲響，宣報海地軍撤出與國旗歸位，多米尼加恢復為一個國家。但恢復只完成了一半：島的東西並存，邊界大致沿馬薩克雷河一帶劃定，兩國此後一百多年共享一條山脈與一條河。土地問題成為新國家最大的內患——海地時期出售的「多米尼加土地」與教會產業的產權歸屬從未獲得正式確認，日後一八六五年復國運動的主要訴求，就是把這批土地要回來。人口方面，大批原本在海地安居的居民返回東部，邊境地帶一度出現大片無人區，這條地緣裂縫在二十世紀初的邊境衝突中又重新浮現。制度上，起義方一八四四年的文告、一八四六年杜阿特出任政府首長、一八六五年他重返並當選總統，逐步把共和憲政的路子鋪了出來；一八六五年復國戰爭中西班牙派兵、美國的干涉先後介入，說明這場島內衝突從來不只是兩國內政。武器與戰術上，這場戰爭也留下了一套「窮國如何對抗強國」的經驗：以游擊替代會戰、以破壞補給線替代消滅敵軍、以小規模集中於關鍵地形贏下一次會戰。這套經驗在一八六五年被直接繼承，只是那一年起義方手裡已是雷管前裝步槍、左輪手槍與輕野砲，武器差距正好被那條外購的渠道抹平。
impactEn: The immediate result was the end of Haiti's twenty-two-year occupation of the east. On 19 July 1844 the bells of the cathedral at Santo Domingo were rung to announce the withdrawal of the Haitian troops and the return of the national flag, and the Dominican lands were once more a country. But the restoration was only half complete: the island remains divided east and west, the frontier was drawn roughly along the Massacre River, and the two states shared one mountain range and one river for more than a century afterwards. The land question became the new state's gravest internal ill: the ownership of the parcels sold during the Haitian occupation as Dominican Crown and ecclesiastical lands was never formally confirmed, and the principal demand of the Restoration movement in 1865 was precisely to have those lands returned. In demographic terms, large numbers who had settled comfortably in Haiti returned to the east, and stretches of the border zone were left empty for a time; that geographic fissure surfaced again in the frontier conflicts of the early twentieth century. Institutionally, the proclamations of 1844, Duarte's taking of the head of government in February 1846 and his return and election as president in 1865 gradually laid out a republican constitutional path; and the fact that Spain sent troops and the United States intervened during the Restoration War of 1865 shows that this island conflict was never a matter of domestic politics alone. In weapons and tactics the war also left behind a set of lessons on how a poor state confronts a strong one: substitutes guerrilla action for pitched battle, substitutes destruction of the enemy's supply line for the destruction of its armies, and wins a single set-piece action by concentrating a small force on the decisive piece of ground. That doctrine was inherited directly in 1865, except that by then the insurgents held percussion muzzle-loading rifles, revolvers and light field guns, and the gap in weapons had been closed by that same line of foreign purchase.
result: 結果分兩層。軍事上，起義方在一八四三年取得塔蘭克雷一役的勝利，卻在七天後失去領袖：杜阿特被俘，聖地亞哥與北部重歸海地軍之手，起義的組織網在搜捕下幾乎被拆散；若只看戰場，一八四三年秋天的起義是失敗的。政治上，起義方卻達成了主要目標：一八四四年海地政局變動後，太子港的新政府判斷佔領的財政與兵員代價已超過收益，同意把軍隊撤到邊界河一線以西，一八二二年以來第一次，東部回到了自己人手中——決定勝負的不是島上的會戰，而是太子港的一次政治計算。長期看，這場戰爭並沒有終止兩國對抗：一八四九年索盧克以海地帝國的姿態大舉入侵，一八五五年海地與西班牙的戰爭把列強拉進加勒比，一八六五年復國戰爭才真正把多米尼加的國家地位鞏固下來。回頭看卡面那支一八四〇年的法國雷管步槍：它從未登上這座島，決定一八四三年勝負的是地形、人數、後勤與一次遠方的政治決定；而它在歐洲解決的問題——濕熱天候下點火不靈、射程延長後隊形散開——恰恰就是這場戰爭裡多米尼加義軍最吃虧的兩個地方，只是他們手上沒有這件東西，要等到一八六五年才用得上。
resultEn: The result has two layers. Militarily, the insurgents won the action at Talanquera in 1843 and lost their leader seven days later: Duarte was taken prisoner, Santiago and the north fell back into Haitian hands, and the organisation of the revolt was almost dismantled by the searches that followed; judged on the field alone, the rising of the autumn of 1843 was a failure. Politically, however, the insurgents achieved their main object. After the change of government in Haiti in 1844, the new authorities at Port-au-Prince judged that the financial and manpower cost of the occupation had exceeded its benefits and agreed to pull the troops back to the west of the border river; for the first time since 1822 the east returned to its own people. What decided the war was not a battle on the island but a political calculation made in Port-au-Prince. In the long run the war did not end the rivalry between the two countries: in 1849 Soulouque invaded on a grand scale as the newly proclaimed emperor of Haiti, the war between Haiti and Spain in 1855 drew the powers into the Caribbean, and only the Restoration War of 1865 finally consolidated the Dominican state. Turning back to the French percussion rifle of 1840 on the card: it never reached this island, and what decided the outcome in 1843 were the ground, the numbers, the lines of supply and a political decision taken far away; the two problems the weapon solved in Europe, unreliable ignition in damp tropical weather and formations breaking up as range increased, were exactly the two places where the Dominican insurgents were worst off, and they simply did not have the weapon in their hands until 1865.
